text: The Patriots' dominant 45-17 demolition of the Raiders in Week 5 provided a rare bright spot amid a mounting injury crisis, as Drake Maye delivered his best performance of the season with five total touchdowns despite missing his top receiver and playing without both starting cornerbacks. However, the victory came at a significant cost: left tackle Will Campbell suffered an MCL sprain in his right knee and is expected to miss game action, while running back TreVeyon Henderson's high ankle sprain will sideline him for multiple weeks, leaving the Patriots' offensive line and backfield in serious flux heading forward. The silver lining is that Maye appears to have finally found his confidence and his deep ball after a rocky start to the season, suggesting the quarterback may be turning a corner even as New England battles to stay healthy on both sides of the ball. Meanwhile, off the field, two Patriots Hall of Famers—Andre Tippett and Julian Edelman—are set to be inducted into the International Jewish Sports Hall of Fame's Class of 2026, adding another distinguished honor to their already legendary legacies.
